answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a refundable bond before accepting jobs, so agents named quill, dune, and opal each need separate collateral. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window and are slashed when a seller signs a delivery receipt whose output fails the job's predefined, verifiable test. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up 1,000 bonds, and cheating risks losing that capital instead of merely discarding free identities.
